analysis.original_request: Design a planar two-layer antireflection coating on a semi-infinite glass substrate (constant refractive index 1.52, lossless), with air incidence (index 1.0). Use only lossless constant-index SiO2 (n=1.46) and TiO2 (n=2.40), one layer of each in either order. Each layer thickness must be between 40 and 160 nm. At normal incidence with s polarization, minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance sampled from 450 to 700 nm at 5 nm spacing. A mean reflectance below 0.03 is the stated target. Use deterministic TMM only, with no RCWA, FDFD, learned surrogate or hardware. Allow at most two executed research rounds with one route and at most 64 solver evaluations per round, seed 17. After observing the actual result, choose a justified adjustment or stop. Do not claim the target was met without the spectrum and independent numeric check.
analysis.normalized_request_english: Design a planar two-layer antireflection coating on a semi-infinite glass substrate (refractive index 1.52, lossless) with air incidence (index 1.0). The stack must consist of exactly one layer of SiO2 (n=1.46) and one layer of TiO2 (n=2.40) in either order, with each layer thickness constrained between 40 and 160 nm. The objective is to minimize the arithmetic mean power reflectance for s-polarized light at normal incidence over the wavelength range 450 to 700 nm (sampled every 5 nm). The stated performance target is a mean reflectance below 0.03, treated as a soft scoring preference. The method must use deterministic Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) only, excluding RCWA, FDFD, surrogates, or hardware acceleration. The optimization process allows at most two research rounds with one route and a maximum of 64 solver evaluations per round using seed 17. Decisions to adjust or stop must be based on observed results and independent numeric checks.
analysis.compatibility_reason: The request requires RCWA, FDTD, or FEM; the Harness supports only laterally uniform planar, linear isotropic, frequency-domain plane-wave layered-media TMM.
